sourceScan.driftSummary: Original canonical excerpts and baseline review describe target revision; current worktree adds authentication, bootstrap, insert fences, upload recovery and cleanup grace/recheck. Aggregate Storage admission remains absent.

assessment.summary: One structural opportunity remains: validate tenant-owned bounded upload admission and a durable object lifecycle to enforce finite per-member quotas; no architectural fix is implemented.

nonNegotiables: Keep storage and gateway authority in the tenant, not the OpenDepartment host.
Keep private read/authentication and column fences.
Do not apply an untested trigger to Supabase-managed Storage tables.
No hosted project actions or architecture implementation in this analysis.
assumptions: No latency, memory or operating budget supplied.
Finite cap should constrain hostile admitted members if presented as a strict guarantee.
Unlimited quota remains an intentional operator setting.

opportunities.title: Own storage admission and object lifetime together
opportunities.summary: Authorize bounded bytes before allocation and own completion/cleanup as a durable lifecycle.
opportunities.diagnosis: Storage admits member bytes while aggregate accounting depends on an optional later client metadata write; cleanup infers abandonment outside that lifetime.

evidence.title: Members can bypass the configured storage quota through direct uploads
evidence.claim: Metadata trigger sums client sizes; Storage insertion independently admits own-folder member objects.

evidence.title: Current quota and Storage policies
evidence.claim: Finite quota still checks public.files rather than Storage allocation.

evidence.title: Separate upload and metadata retry path
evidence.claim: Bytes precede metadata; stable-path retry now preserves uncertain writes.

evidence.title: Orphan grace and purge recheck
evidence.claim: Age filtering and requery narrow stale cleanup, but list and delete remain separate.

evidence.title: Cleanup age and reference regression
evidence.claim: Recent-orphan test failed before SQL grace; after change all148 tenant and52 control assertions passed. This is SQL-shim evidence only.

evidence.title: Separated allocation and lifecycle ownership
evidence.claim: The quota and cleanup weaknesses share absent ownership of admission, completion and deletion states.

desiredInvariants: Confirmed bytes plus reserved capacity stay within finite cap at admission, including concurrent requests.
Every stored object has one member/path reservation and no alternate unaccounted write route.
Trusted byte consumer enforces reservation bound independently of client claims.
Completion is idempotent and creates trusted size metadata.
Deleting objects cannot complete; capacity releases only after confirmed removal/absence.
Pending/deleting states remain charged, visible and retryable.

options.title: Metadata accounting with stronger recovery
options.summary: Preserve direct browser uploads, stable-path retries and one-hour orphan grace with a purge recheck.

findingCoverage.title: Members can bypass the configured storage quota through direct uploads
findingCoverage.rationale: Direct uploads and client size claims remain outside metadata accounting.

evidenceCoverage.title: Separate upload and metadata retry path
evidenceCoverage.rationale: Stable-path recovery and grace/recheck narrow accidental loss; final cross-service race remains.

evidenceCoverage.title: Orphan grace and purge recheck
evidenceCoverage.rationale: Stable-path recovery and grace/recheck narrow accidental loss; final cross-service race remains.

tradeoffs.assessment: Improves accidental-loss containment only; canonical malicious-member quota bypass remains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run direct-upload/false-size scenarios and current retry/grace regressions; do not expect quota bypass to close.

tradeoffs.assessment: Successful byte path remains direct; extra queries occur on retry or cleanup.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare direct upload p50/p95 and recovery query count at small and maximum file size.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new runtime or server-side streaming buffers; existing browser File handling remains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure browser heap during file selection and retry; check no retained file growth across repeated selections.

tradeoffs.assessment: Retry reconciliation reduces duplicate/missing metadata, but list/delete remains separate.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject lost metadata replies and delayed metadata completion during cleanup.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing app and schema release; operators need visible cleanup failures.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise failed Storage listing/delete and verify actionable retry feedback.

tradeoffs.assessment: Current RPC shape remains compatible; reapply tenant SQL and deploy client.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run old/new clients against reapplied schema and preserve RPC shape.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing split APIs stay familiar but future callers can omit recovery.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review a new upload caller for duplicated metadata cleanup logic.

tradeoffs.assessment: Independent UI changes are reversible; keep grace/recovery protections.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse client downgrade while keeping schema safety guards.

residualRisks: Malicious admitted member can bypass finite cap with direct upload or false size.
Grace and recheck do not make list/delete atomic.

workPackages: Retain retry, age-grace and purge recheck fixes; document soft quota.
acceptanceCriteria: UI does not promise strict aggregate enforcement.
migrationNotes: Keep current authentication and column-privilege fixes independently.
No architecture implementation selected or performed.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Retain safety guards while reverting independent UI presentation if needed.

options.title: Tenant-owned admission, reservations and bounded upload gateway
options.summary: Tenant-local gateway reserves capacity under member lock, independently limits streamed bytes, denies direct Storage writes and owns durable completion/deletion states.

findingCoverage.title: Members can bypass the configured storage quota through direct uploads
findingCoverage.rationale: Conditional on implementing bounded admission and denying all direct writes; proposal alone does not close finding.

evidenceCoverage.title: Separate upload and metadata retry path
evidenceCoverage.rationale: Durable idempotent completion and deleting states own metadata/object lifetime; keep current guards while legacy paths drain.

evidenceCoverage.title: Orphan grace and purge recheck
evidenceCoverage.rationale: Durable idempotent completion and deleting states own metadata/object lifetime; keep current guards while legacy paths drain.

tradeoffs.assessment: Moves finite-cap admission before consumption and lifecycle under one owner; privileged gateway introduces new attack surface.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: In hosted synthetic tenant, test all direct write routes, false lengths, over-bound streams, replay, cross-member paths and old signed capabilities.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds admission and streaming hops plus same-member lock contention.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark current/candidate uploads with one/many members, small/max files and slow clients; agree p95/throughput/lock-wait budgets before rollout.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds bounded stream buffers, reservation rows/indexes and charged pending objects.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure gateway peak memory/backpressure, pending row growth and stored bytes under abort storms; reject unbounded growth.

tradeoffs.assessment: Durable idempotent recovery prevents premature release; gateway or worker failure delays admissions/reclamation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Crash at each reserve/upload/finalize/delete/release boundary and check invariants with concurrent native sessions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires per-tenant deployment, credentials, worker health and stuck-state repair.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Practice worker outage/restart, credential rotation and stuck-reservation recovery without logging tokens/content.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires trusted object inventory, old-client coordination, policy cutover and write pause.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Dry-run inventory and cutover on referenced/orphan/missing-object fixtures; verify direct writes denied before reopening.

tradeoffs.assessment: One lifecycle API reduces caller drift, with more state-machine complexity.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Implement a test upload caller through the API; ensure it cannot mutate accounting or lifecycle out of order.

tradeoffs.assessment: Rollback requires pausing uploads and resolving charged states; unrestricted policy restores only soft quota.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse pause/drain/reconcile/revert without completed-object loss or silently retaining a strict quota claim.

residualRisks: Gateway credential compromise has tenant-wide potential impact where only broad service keys exist.
Provider upload/delete semantics, bounded streaming feasibility and old signed capabilities need hosted validation.
Remote Storage and SQL commits remain separate; durable charged pending state is required.

affectedComponents: Proposed tenant-owned gateway and cleanup worker
workPackages: Define lifecycle contract and role grants.
Prototype hosted bounded streaming and deny direct writes.
Implement locked reservations and idempotent completion/deletion.
Inventory objects, rehearse migration and pilot opt-in tenant.
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent finite-cap admission never exceeds charged capacity.
Direct unreserved writes and false-size streams are rejected.
Completed objects survive retries; deleting reservations cannot finalize.
Budget is released only after confirmed deletion/absence.
migrationNotes: Keep current authentication and column-privilege fixes independently.
No architecture implementation selected or performed.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Pause admissions, drain or clean pending states, reconcile stored bytes; restore old API only with explicit soft-quota contract.

opportunities.recommendation: Validate tenant-owned admission if finite quotas must resist malicious members; retain metadata recovery as immediate baseline or final soft-quota option when operational simplicity dominates.

openQuestions: Tenant streaming/worker runtime and operating budget?
Narrower gateway authority than a broad tenant service key?
Hosted deletion/partial-upload acknowledgment and old signed-capability semantics?
Reservation lifetime and stuck-state recovery policy?
Strict finite-cap guarantee or explicitly cooperative usage allowance?
validationLimitations: No hosted Supabase service was contacted.
PGlite does not reproduce the hosted upload/delete protocol or multi-session concurrency.
Canonical draft hashes identify inspected inputs, not sealed integrity.
Proposal requires option selection, source refresh and hosted validation before implementation.
